questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The selected country was an English-speaking country. I also thought that the University of Otago had a lot of interesting subjects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really an amazing experience, and I would recommend every student try to go on an exchange. You learn a lot from other international students and get an insight into how things are done differently in other countries.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was a bit tricky to find all the different information from the host university, but I think it is because many things are done differently and are called something else. But once I figured out the systems, it went very smoothly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Well we had a couple of introduction sessions with all the international students, which was helpful. They explained everything, from student insurance to exam format, to how the uni systems worked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were very helpful. I didn't need any more help, but I knew exactly where to request it if I did.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy; I found the accommodation through UniFlats, which is part of the University. I was placed with four other international students in a nice house near the campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Technically it is off campus, but every student house is within 5-10 minutes walk from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Well, because I was an exchange student, I had to ask for permission for all my papers. That process was a bit technical, and I was also initially confused about whether I had to choose a program, but the host university quickly reached out and explained how I should apply.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember it in close details, but you first had to apply to a program, which for all one semester abroad students was Certificate of Proficiency – Exchange. And then after that you had to select the papers/courses you wanted to take part in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had the opportunity to write an email and ask questions. I think I had one question about the program application, and they answered within one day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into the courses, and do not be afraid to send an email with questions. They are there to help you, and they are very happy to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was pleasantly surprised by the academic level. A lot of my friends who went to, for example, the States have said that they were disappointed with the level abroad, but I found all my courses very good and learning.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one BA course (300 level) and 3 MA houses (400 level).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was more student participation, most likely because fewer students were in my classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economics of Health and Education, Monetary Economics, The Economics of Natural Resources and Public Choice, and Topics in Advanced Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! All had brilliant teachers! My favourite was probably Economics of Health and Education and Topics in Advanced Economics. Monetary Economics is good, but on a high level, as you have to do four 30-35-minute presentations on your own during the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not anything in particular.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Well, NZ is generally an expensive country, so food is a bit more expensive than DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had a lot of opportunities; they hosted some events for us where we could get to know the other international students. And we had free gym facilities, including badminton, basket, football and so forth.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any, but there was plenty; I got all the invitations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do some sports, they have all sorts of free activities you can do like badminton, basketball and volleyball.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on some trips, do some hiking, there are plenty of opportunities around the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to some of them in class, ask questions, eat lunch with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In the master class, you have to actively participate, and there are a lot of presentations, and you quickly become better in English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked all of it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded, and try to socialise with the other international students. Going to classes improves the whole experience; the teachers are very nice and friendly. Go on some trips during your free time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience and live in another county for a longer period of time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: During so many English presentations, it really taught me a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
